evidence: Architecture plan integrated from planner st_01a06cf8: use a framework-neutral ApplicationFacade plus immutable ProgressEvent/ProgressReporter, GenerationOutcome, and thread-safe CancellationToken; run synchronous facade operations in one Textual thread worker and forward events via call_from_thread. Wave 1 contracts; Wave 2 disjoint parallel lanes for generation/cancellation, NotebookLM process lifecycle, XDG settings, and DirectoryTree picker; Wave 3 facade/composition plus TUI shell/screens; Wave 4 CLI migration plus packaging/entrypoints/docs; Wave 5 integration and final audit. Recommended dependency is textual>=8.2.8,<9 for Python 3.10, plus platformdirs>=4,<5; no picker dependency. Risks recorded: event-loop blocking, unkillable workers/orphan subprocesses, cancellation races, retry sleeps, Unicode paths, empty directories, resize, and stale CSV output collisions.

goals.objective: Migrate /home/avell/Projects/unchain0/flashcards-generator to a production-quality Textual TUI on Python 3.10. Reuse existing domain/application/infrastructure/adapters and current AnkiConnect, CSV, NotebookLM behavior; do not duplicate business logic in screens/widgets. C004 NotebookLM/Settings/Picker: Pilot covers auth state, login delegation, cleanup-all confirmation, XDG load/save/invalid fallback, and keyboard directory navigation including Unicode/spaces/empty folders. C005 usability/manual surface: real xterm.js-rendered TUI screenshots/transcript at wide and narrow terminal sizes prove visible tabs/footer/shortcuts, no overflow, and no log dumping; exercise happy, invalid, and cancel actions. C006 regression/quality: full existing suite plus TUI tests, ruff/format, mypy, build, and project quality gates exit zero. Every behavioral criterion needs failing-first Textual Pilot/integration or real PTY evidence; documentation gets review/read QA. Stop only when all criteria are RED-to-GREEN, manual artifacts and cleanup receipts exist, final quality is green, independent audit is complete, and ulw-loop marks this objective complete.
